workstream: WS3 — simulator answer-provenance ledger + builtin judge (proposal V2-1)
summary: Persist one JSONL record per intercepted AskUserQuestion — {ts, question, options, answer, tier: override|llm|fallback, hook_model, match, llm_raw, error, temperature_stripped} — plus explicit disabled-records on BOTH silent-disable paths, written by the PreToolUse interceptor to Path(__file__).parent/hook_answers.jsonl (never CWD, fixing in-repo repo pollution). Harvest it per case and at the run root (batch), expose it to judges as outputs["hook_answers"] with a load-bearing None-vs-[] distinction plus interception_configured and hook_answers_scope flags, ship a builtin bool judge process/simulator_provenance that fails on fallback/disabled/error records AND on a missing ledger when interception is configured and the trace shows AskUserQuestion calls, and render a per-case "Simulated user" line in report.html. All 6 corrections from the V2-1 verdict are incorporated. Gating reuses existing thresholds machinery (min_pass_rate: 1.0) — no new eval.yaml keys. Out of scope (documented as such): harvesting the in-container ledger on the Harbor path (agent_eval/harbor/results.py follow-up — the judge fails honestly there rather than false-greening) and fixing the pre-existing in-repo tool_handlers.yaml CWD-resolution breakage (the new disabled-record surfaces it).

changes.spec: Ledger writer, anchored to the script's own directory (verdict correction 1). (a) After the stdlib imports (before the `try: import yaml` at line 31) add `from datetime import datetime, timezone`, module constant `_LEDGER = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "hook_answers.jsonl"`, and `def _log_answer(record: dict) -> None`: best-effort append — `record.setdefault("ts", datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"))`, open(_LEDGER, "a", encoding="utf-8"), write json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n", entire body in `try/except Exception: pass` (the never-crash constraint at lines 20-29: a crashed PreToolUse hook silently disables ALL interception). Docstring notes O_APPEND single-line writes are interleaving-safe for practical line sizes in batch mode. _LEDGER lands at <case_ws>/hooks/ in case AND in-repo mode (workspace.py:317, 534-538) and <workspace>/hooks/ in batch mode (workspace.py:204) — never the user's repo (execute.py:716,724-745). (b) PyYAML ImportError path (lines 31-43): before sys.exit(0), call _log_answer({"tier": "disabled", "reason": "pyyaml-missing"}) — possible because _log_answer is defined above and uses only json/Path/datetime (verdict correction 2). (c) main() missing-config path (lines 52-54): before sys.exit(0), _log_answer({"tier": "disabled", "reason": "tool-handlers-missing", "cwd": os.getcwd()}) — the cwd field surfaces the pre-existing in-repo breakage where Path("tool_handlers.yaml") is unresolvable at repo CWD. (d) `_create_message(client, meta=None, **kwargs)`: new optional meta dict, NOT forwarded to client.messages.create; on the temperature-strip retry set meta["temperature_stripped"] = True. Existing callers/tests unaffected (positional client + kwargs unchanged). (e) `_llm_answer(question, options, handler_prompt, model=None)` now returns a 2-tuple `(label_or_None, meta)` (verdict issue 4 acknowledged: return-shape change): meta = {"model": resolved_model} where resolved_model = model or "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"; pass meta into _create_message; on exact label match set meta["match"]="exact", on fuzzy match "fuzzy"; on rejected reply set meta["llm_raw"]=answer[:500] and return (None, meta); on exception set meta["error"]=str(e)[:500] and return (None, meta). Keep all existing stderr prints. (f) `_handle_ask_user` answer loop (141-162): build entry = {"question": text, "options": [o.get("label","") for o in options if isinstance(o, dict)]}; tier resolution unchanged but records tier: "override" when case_overrides hits; unpack `answer, llm_meta = _llm_answer(...)` and set tier "llm" when answer is not None; fallback branch (existing stderr warning preserved) sets tier "fallback". When llm_meta exists (llm tier OR fallback-after-LLM-attempt) copy hook_model=llm_meta["model"] and any of match/llm_raw/error/temperature_stripped into entry. Set entry["answer"]=answer, call _log_answer(entry) per question, then answers[text]=answer as before. Edge: no options and no override → tier fallback answer "yes", no llm_meta. Deny-path and Bash/env handlers write NO records (scope: AskUserQuestion + disabled only).

New helper `_collect_case_ledger(src_root: Path, dest_dir: Path) -> bool`: src = src_root/"hooks"/"hook_answers.jsonl"; return False unless src.is_file() and not src.is_symlink() and not src.parent.is_symlink() and src.resolve().is_relative_to(src_root.resolve()) (CWE-59 — workspace is agent-writable, mirroring _collect_modified_files' containment at 440-453); else mkdir dest_dir and shutil.copy2(src, dest_dir/"hook_answers.jsonl"), return True. Called from (a) `_collect_per_case` per-case loop, next to the _generate_events_json call (~line 232): `if _collect_case_ledger(case_dir, output_dir / "cases" / case_id): results.setdefault(case_id, {})["hook_answers"] = 1` — covers case mode AND in-repo mode (both keep the ledger at <case_ws>/hooks/); (b) batch branch of main(), before the collection-summary write at ~line 133: `if _collect_case_ledger(workspace, output_dir): print("  hook ledger: hook_answers.jsonl (run-level)")` (verdict correction 3 — batch ledger goes to the RUN ROOT, mirroring the run-root events.json written at line 143). (a) New module helper `_parse_hook_ledger(path: Path) -> list | None`: read text (utf-8, errors=replace); return None on OSError (file exists but unreadable → provenance unknown → fail-safe); parse line-per-line with json.loads, skip blank/malformed lines (one stderr warning per file), keep only dicts; returns [] for an empty file. (b) In `load_case_record` (196), insert after the events block (~line 361), mirroring the events run-root fallback at 331-337 exactly: set record["interception_configured"] = bool(config.inputs.tools) (config.py:308-311); ledger_path = case_dir/"hook_answers.jsonl", scope "case"; if absent and run_id and runs_dir → candidate = runs_dir/run_id/"hook_answers.jsonl", scope "run" (batch: run-level, unattributed); if a path exists → record["hook_answers"] = _parse_hook_ledger(path) and record["hook_answers_scope"] = scope (scope None if parse returned None); else record["hook_answers"] = None, record["hook_answers_scope"] = None. New builtin bool python judge (stdlib-only; auto-discovered by BuiltinJudgeRegistry and the config-load filesystem scan — zero config wiring, config.py:1326-1330 accepts `builtin: simulator_provenance` or `process/simulator_provenance`). Docstring (verdict correction 6, mandatory wording): states a pass certifies *answer-provenance coverage only* — every intercepted answer came from a recorded tier (override/llm) and interception was never silently disabled — and explicitly NOT simulator calibration: tier=llm answers are reported, not validated against human answers (paper P1's reporting clause, not its calibration clause). Documents 'Required fields: hook_answers, interception_configured, events', 'Failure means: ...', the hook-crash blind spot (a crashed PreToolUse hook is CLI pass-through and cannot write from inside; the missing-ledger check is its detectable signature — verdict correction 2), and the batch-mode run-level scope note. Helper `_count_ask_user(events) -> (calls, questions)`: iterate events, type=="assistant", tools list, name=="AskUserQuestion"; questions += len(input["questions"]) when input is a dict with a non-empty questions list else 1 (parse_stream_events' _cap_values preserves dict structure, events.py:407-412). `judge(outputs, **kwargs)` logic: configured = bool(outputs.get("interception_configured")); ledger = outputs.get("hook_answers"); scope = outputs.get("hook_answers_scope"). CASE ledger is None: pass with 'No tool interception configured' when not configured; FAIL when configured and calls > 0 ('no ledger collected but trace shows N AskUserQuestion call(s) — simulated-user provenance unrecorded: hook crash, pre-ledger interceptor, or collection gap') — verdict correction 4 verbatim; pass ('nothing to certify') when configured but zero AskUserQuestion calls. CASE ledger is a list: tier counts n_override/n_llm/n_fallback/n_disabled; problems list gathers (1) disabled records with deduped reasons, (2) fallback records with up to 5 question texts (each truncated ~80 chars) plus their error/llm_raw cause when present, (3) any non-fallback record carrying error, (4) coverage: when scope != "run" and questions > 0 and answered_count < questions → 'partial provenance' failure (catches swallowed best-effort writes and an empty-but-present ledger with observed questions); skipped for run scope where per-case attribution is impossible. Fail with '; '.join(problems) + tier summary; pass rationale = 'All N answer(s) from recorded tiers (tiers: X override / Y llm)' — always appending ' [run-level ledger — batch mode, answers not attributed to cases]' when scope == "run" (verdict correction 3). Returns (bool, str) like process/tool_call_validation.py. No arguments.

Should this workstream also FIX it (resolve tool_handlers.yaml relative to Path(__file__).parent.parent as a fallback — enabling interception in in-repo evals for the first time, a behavior change), or only surface it as designed and file a follow-up?
